param.num_paths.label: Number of strokes
param.num_paths.help: How many Bézier strokes the sketch has. This controls the level of abstraction: few strokes = very abstract, many strokes = detailed. (Original: --num_strokes / --num_paths)
param.num_iter.label: Iterations
param.num_iter.help: Optimisation steps per sketch. The paper uses 2001. More iterations = cleaner lines but longer runtime. Stops early when converged.
param.num_sketches.label: Number of sketches
param.num_sketches.help: Several sketches are drawn with different seeds (0, 1000, 2000 …) and the one with the lowest loss is picked automatically. Recommended: 3.
param.seed.label: Start seed
param.seed.help: Random seed of the first sketch. Further sketches use seed + 1000, + 2000 … Same seed + same settings = reproducible result.
param.best_by.label: Best sketch
param.best_by.help: Which of the sketches counts as the best (★). “Most similar”: the one most like the photo – as before. “Similar & beautiful (experimental)”: among the sketches at most 3 CLIP points behind the most similar one, the look counts too (LAION’s aesthetic score – trained on photos; on sketches it prefers cleaner lines, no more). “My taste”: likeness and your thumbs up/down – from 10 ratings on, until then like “Most similar”.
param.mask_object.label: Remove background
param.mask_object.help: Automatically removes the image background before drawing (the object is found by the mask model). Recommended for photos with a background.
param.fix_scale.label: Keep aspect ratio
param.fix_scale.help: Non-square images are padded to a square with white borders instead of being stretched or cropped.
param.image_scale.label: Working resolution
param.image_scale.help: Canvas size in pixels. CLIP works at 224 px internally; larger values draw finer but are slower.
param.width.label: Stroke width
param.width.help: Width of every stroke in pixels (relative to the working resolution).
param.num_segments.label: Segments per stroke
param.num_segments.help: How many connected curve pieces a stroke consists of. 1 = a single Bézier curve (paper).
param.control_points_per_seg.label: Curve type
param.control_points_per_seg.help: Points per segment: 2 = straight line, 3 = quadratic, 4 = cubic Bézier curve (paper).
param.path_svg.label: Initial SVG
param.path_svg.help: Optional: an existing SVG sketch to start from. Its strokes are optimised further; missing strokes up to the requested number are added.
param.attention_init.label: Attention initialisation
param.attention_init.help: Initial stroke positions are placed on the most salient image regions (saliency map) instead of randomly. Much better results.
param.saliency_model.label: Saliency model
param.saliency_model.help: What computes the attention map: CLIP (relevance map, paper) or DINO (self-attention of a ViT-S/8).
param.saliency_clip_model.label: CLIP model for saliency
param.saliency_clip_model.help: CLIP variant for the attention map. ViT models use attention relevance, ResNet models use Grad-CAM with the text target.
param.xdog_intersec.label: Intersect with edges (XDoG)
param.xdog_intersec.help: The attention map is multiplied with an XDoG edge image so strokes start on edges.
param.mask_object_attention.label: Mask for start points
param.mask_object_attention.help: Place initial stroke positions only on the object (object mask). "Automatic" = same as "Remove background".
param.softmax_temp.label: Softmax temperature
param.softmax_temp.help: How strongly the start points concentrate on the most important spots. Small = very concentrated, large = more evenly spread.
param.text_target.label: Text target
param.text_target.help: Optional text (e.g. "a camel"). Used by the ResNet Grad-CAM saliency and by text guidance. Empty = none.
param.clip_model_name.label: CLIP model (loss)
param.clip_model_name.help: CLIP network whose features compare sketch and photo. RN101 is the paper default. Other models may need a one-time download.
param.clip_conv_loss.label: Geometric CLIP loss
param.clip_conv_loss.help: Compares intermediate CLIP layers (geometry) and the output (semantics). The core of CLIPasso – only switch off for experiments.
param.clip_conv_loss_type.label: Distance
param.clip_conv_loss_type.help: Distance between intermediate features: L2 (paper), L1 or cosine.
param.clip_conv_layer_weights.label: CLIP layer weights
param.clip_conv_layer_weights.help: Weight of every intermediate layer in the geometric loss. Early layers = fine geometry, late layers = coarse shapes. Paper: 0, 0, 1, 1, 0.
param.clip_fc_loss_weight.label: Semantic loss weight
param.clip_fc_loss_weight.help: Weight of the CLIP output (semantics). Higher = the sketch stays recognisable even if the geometry deviates. Paper: 0.1.
param.train_with_clip.label: Additional CLIP loss (ViT-B/32)
param.train_with_clip.help: Adds a semantic loss with CLIP ViT-B/32 (cosine distance to the photo).
param.clip_weight.label: CLIP loss weight
param.clip_weight.help: Weight of the additional CLIP loss.
param.start_clip.label: CLIP loss from iteration
param.start_clip.help: The additional CLIP loss is activated from this iteration on.
param.include_target_in_aug.label: Include un-augmented sketch
param.include_target_in_aug.help: Also puts the un-augmented sketch into the batch of the additional CLIP loss.
param.clip_text_guide.label: Text guidance (weight)
param.clip_text_guide.help: Additionally pulls the sketch towards the text target (CLIP text-image similarity). 0 = off.
param.percep_loss.label: Perceptual loss
param.percep_loss.help: Optional extra loss: L2 (pixels) or LPIPS (VGG16 features).
param.perceptual_weight.label: Perceptual loss weight
param.perceptual_weight.help: Weight of the perceptual loss. 0 = no effect.
param.lr.label: Learning rate
param.lr.help: Step size for moving the control points (in pixels). Paper: 1.0.
param.lr_scheduler.label: Learning-rate decay
param.lr_scheduler.help: Exponentially decays the learning rate down to 10 % at the end of the optimisation.
param.force_sparse.label: Optimise opacity (sparse)
param.force_sparse.help: Also optimises the opacity of every stroke so that unnecessary strokes fade out.
param.color_lr.label: Opacity learning rate
param.color_lr.help: Learning rate for the stroke opacity.
param.color_vars_threshold.label: Minimum opacity
param.color_vars_threshold.help: Strokes with a lower opacity are left out when saving.
param.num_stages.label: Training stages
param.num_stages.help: Multi-stage drawing: every stage adds new strokes and freezes the previous ones. Total = strokes × stages.
param.eval_interval.label: Evaluation interval
param.eval_interval.help: Every how many iterations the loss is evaluated without augmentation and the best sketch is saved.
param.save_interval.label: Save a step every … iterations
param.save_interval.help: How often an intermediate state is saved. The animation “drawing process” shows these steps: 1 = every iteration (the finest animation, a little more disk space), 10 = every tenth (paper).
param.augemntations.label: Augmentations
param.augemntations.help: Random distortions so CLIP compares robust features: affine (perspective + crop, paper) and noise on the control points.
param.num_aug_clip.label: Augmentations per step
param.num_aug_clip.help: How many augmented copies are compared with CLIP per iteration. More = more stable but slower. Paper: 4.
param.augment_both.label: Augment the photo too
param.augment_both.help: The same distortion is applied to sketch and photo (paper). Off = only the sketch is distorted.
param.aug_scale_min.label: Crop scale
param.aug_scale_min.help: Size of the random crop relative to the image (original code: 0.8).
param.noise_thresh.label: Noise threshold
param.noise_thresh.help: Probability threshold for noise on the control points (higher = less often).
param.device.label: Compute device
param.device.help: Automatic uses an NVIDIA GPU if available (GPU edition only), otherwise the CPU.
param.gpunum.label: GPU index
param.gpunum.help: Which GPU to use if there are several.
param.multiprocess.label: Always compute in parallel
param.multiprocess.help: Always computes several sketches at the same time in their own processes (needs about 2–3 GB of memory per sketch). Without it, a CPU with 6 or more cores does this by itself when there is enough memory (Settings).
param.num_threads.label: CPU threads
param.num_threads.help: Number of CPU threads for PyTorch. 0 = automatic.

ui.about.byline: By: Junostr05 – app idea, GUI vision and UI/UX direction
ui.about.desc: CLIPasso Studio brings together four methods that draw vector sketches from photos: CLIPasso (SIGGRAPH 2022) optimises Bézier strokes until CLIP “sees” the sketch like the photo; SwiftSketch (SIGGRAPH 2025) generates the strokes in seconds with a diffusion model; ControlSketch optimises them with Stable Diffusion and ControlNet for especially natural sketches; SceneSketch (CLIPascene, ICCV 2023) sketches whole scenes with background as a matrix of abstraction levels. The “Compare” page puts the methods side by side for one image.
ui.about.credits_text:
CLIPasso: Semantically-Aware Object Sketching – Yael Vinker, Ehsan Pajouheshgar, Jessica Y. Bo, Roman Christian Bachmann, Amit Haim Bermano, Daniel Cohen-Or, Amir Zamir, Ariel Shamir (ACM TOG / SIGGRAPH 2022).
SwiftSketch: A Diffusion Model for Image-to-Vector Sketch Generation (with ControlSketch) – Ellie Arar, Yarden Frenkel, Daniel Cohen-Or, Ariel Shamir, Yael Vinker (SIGGRAPH 2025). SwiftSketch and ControlSketch are re-implemented independently here; the SwiftSketch weights are the authors'.
CLIPascene: Scene Sketching with Different Types and Levels of Abstraction (SceneSketch) – Yael Vinker, Yuval Alaluf, Daniel Cohen-Or, Ariel Shamir (ICCV 2023), ported from the MIT-licensed original code.

Uses: CLIP (OpenAI), BiRefNet, U²-Net, DINO, Stable Diffusion 1.5, ControlNet, LaMa, MiDaS DPT, BLIP, diffusers, transformers, PyTorch, Qt for Python, Inter, Lucide. The differentiable renderer is a PyTorch re-implementation of diffvg.
ui.about.license_text: CLIPasso is licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 – non-commercial use only. This app uses the same licence. The SwiftSketch weights are provided by the authors (without an explicit licence – research/personal use only); Stable Diffusion 1.5 / ControlNet are licensed under CreativeML OpenRAIL-M; SceneSketch (MIT) and LaMa (Apache-2.0) are open source. method.clipasso.tagline: Optimises strokes with CLIP – the classic, highly configurable
method.clipasso.desc: CLIPasso (SIGGRAPH 2022) optimises Bézier strokes until CLIP “sees” the sketch like the photo. Lots of options, runs on CPU and GPU.
method.swiftsketch.desc: SwiftSketch (SIGGRAPH 2025) generates the strokes with a diffusion model in 50 denoising steps and refines them afterwards. Very fast, even on the CPU. The model weights (≈ 710 MB) are downloaded on first use.
method.controlsketch.tagline: Stable Diffusion + ControlNet – best quality, needs a GPU
method.controlsketch.desc: ControlSketch optimises the strokes with an SDS loss from Stable Diffusion 1.5 steered by a ControlNet (depth, edges …). Very detailed, natural sketches – practical only with an NVIDIA GPU (≈ 3–4 GB of models).

param.swiftsketch.num_sketches.help: Several sketches are generated with different seeds (20, 1020, 2020 …); the one with the highest CLIP score is picked automatically. Each sketch takes only seconds.
param.swiftsketch.seed.help: Random seed of the initial noise of the first sketch (original: 20). Further sketches use seed + 1000, + 2000 …
param.swiftsketch.mask_object.help: Removes the background (mask model) before the image features are computed (the original always masks). Recommended.
param.guidance_param.label: Guidance strength
param.guidance_param.help: Classifier-free guidance: how closely the diffusion model follows the image. 1 = no guidance, 2.5 = original. Higher values stick closer to the photo but can get busier.
param.use_refine.label: Refinement network
param.use_refine.help: Smooths and corrects the strokes after the diffusion with the refinement network (full SwiftSketch pipeline). Off = the diffusion result only.
param.save_diffusion_sketch.label: Also save the diffusion sketch
param.save_diffusion_sketch.help: Additionally saves the sketch before refinement as diffusion_sketch.svg in the result folder.
param.swiftsketch.width.help: Stroke width of the output sketch in pixels (224 × 224 canvas). Only affects the rendering, not the strokes.
param.num_strokes.label: Number of strokes
param.num_strokes.help: How many strokes the sketch has – sets the level of abstraction. Original: 32.
param.controlsketch.num_iter.help: Optimisation steps with the SDS loss. Original: 2000. On a GPU ≈ 0.1–0.3 s per step.
param.controlsketch.num_sketches.help: Several sketches with different seeds (0, 1000, 2000 …); the one with the highest CLIP score is picked.
param.controlsketch.seed.help: Random seed (stroke start points and SDS noise). Further sketches use seed + 1000, + 2000 …
param.caption.label: Caption (prompt)
param.caption.help: Text for Stable Diffusion, e.g. “a camel standing in the desert”. Empty = generated automatically with BLIP.
param.controlsketch.fix_scale.help: Non-square images are padded to a square with white borders instead of being stretched.
param.object_size_ratio.label: Object size while drawing
param.object_size_ratio.help: While drawing, the object is reduced to at most this fraction of the canvas and scaled back to its original size at the end. Original: 0.75.
param.render_size.label: Working resolution
param.render_size.help: Size of the canvas in pixels that is optimised (Stable Diffusion 1.5 is trained for 512).
param.output_svg_size.label: SVG output size
param.output_svg_size.help: Size of the output SVG in pixels; strokes and stroke width are scaled accordingly.
param.controlsketch.width.help: Stroke width in pixels on the working canvas. Original: 2.5.
param.sort_final_sketch.label: Sort strokes
param.sort_final_sketch.help: Sorts the strokes at the end: first those along the object outline, then by attention. Useful for animations and partial sketches.
param.use_init_method.label: Attention initialisation
param.use_init_method.help: Stroke start points are chosen from an attention map with a weighted K-means instead of at random.
param.attn_model.label: Attention model
param.attn_model.help: CLIP (bundled) or the cross-attention of Stable Diffusion XL for the object name (optional download ≈ 7 GB, original default). On graphics cards with less than 8 GB this step computes piece by piece on the card or on the processor.
param.object_name.label: Object name
param.object_name.help: Word for the SDXL attention, e.g. “camel”. Empty = CLIP attention.
param.condition.label: ControlNet condition
param.condition.help: Which structure of the photo steers the strokes: depth (original default), edges (Canny), soft edges (HED), scribble, segmentation or normals.
param.conditioning_scale.label: ControlNet strength
param.conditioning_scale.help: How strongly the ControlNet influences the diffusion. Original: 0.15.
param.diffusion_guidance_scale.label: Guidance strength (SDS)
param.diffusion_guidance_scale.help: Classifier-free guidance of the SDS loss. SDS needs high values; original: 100.
param.diffusion_timesteps.label: Max. diffusion timestep
param.diffusion_timesteps.help: Upper bound of the random noise timesteps (between 50 and min(950, value)). Original: 1000.
param.controlsketch.lr.help: Step size for moving the control points (in pixels). Original: 0.8.
param.controlsketch.save_interval.help: How often an intermediate state is saved. The animation “drawing process” shows these steps: 1 = every iteration (the finest animation, a little more disk space), 100 = every hundredth (paper). The CLIP score is computed about every 100 iterations either way.

method.scenesketch.tagline: Whole scenes with background – a matrix of abstraction levels
method.scenesketch.desc: SceneSketch (CLIPascene, ICCV 2023) sketches a whole scene: the foreground object and the background (filled in with LaMa) are drawn separately and combined. It produces a matrix of sketches – from precise to loose (fidelity: CLIP layers) and from detailed to sparse (simplicity). Minutes per sketch on a GPU, much longer on the CPU. Downloads LaMa (≈ 200 MB) on first use.
ui.preset_hint.scenesketch.fast: Layer 8 only, no simplification, 1 seed – one scene sketch (≈ 20 min on a CPU, 1–2 min on a GPU).
ui.preset_hint.scenesketch.standard: Layer 8 with 4 simplification levels, 1 seed – one column of the matrix.
ui.preset_hint.scenesketch.quality: Settings of the paper: layers 2, 8, 11 × 8 simplification levels, 2 seeds – the full 3 × 9 matrix. Hours, even on a GPU.
param.scenesketch.layers.label: Fidelity layers
param.scenesketch.layers.help: One sketch column per selected CLIP ViT-B/32 layer. Shallow layers (2, 3, 4) follow the geometry of the photo closely, deep layers (8, 11) keep only what the scene is about and draw more loosely. Paper: 2, 8, 11.
param.scenesketch.simplicity_levels.help: How many increasingly sparse versions of every fidelity sketch are made (0 = none). Every level removes strokes from the previous one. Paper: 8; fewer levels cover the same range in bigger steps.
param.scenesketch.num_strokes.label: Number of strokes
param.scenesketch.num_strokes.help: Strokes of the background sketch and of the object sketch each (before simplification). Paper: 64.
param.scenesketch.num_sketches.help: Every sketch and every simplification level is optimised with this many seeds (0, 1000, …); the best one is kept (lowest loss). Paper: 2.
param.scenesketch.seed.help: Random seed of the first run. Further runs use seed + 1000, + 2000 …
param.scenesketch.split_scene.label: Separate object and background
param.scenesketch.split_scene.help: The foreground object (found by the mask model) and the background (object area filled in with LaMa) are sketched separately and combined – the method of the paper. Off: the whole image is sketched as one.
param.scenesketch.resize_obj.label: Enlarge the object for sketching
param.scenesketch.resize_obj.help: A single, small object is enlarged to 70 % of the canvas while it is sketched and scaled back afterwards – more detail on small objects (original: on for objects).
param.scenesketch.fix_scale.help: Non-square images are padded to a square with white borders. Off: they are cropped to the centre (SceneSketch works on square images).
param.scenesketch.num_iter.label: Iterations (background)
param.scenesketch.num_iter.help: Optimisation steps of every fidelity sketch of the background (or of the whole image). Original: 1501.
param.scenesketch.object_num_iter.label: Iterations (object)
param.scenesketch.object_num_iter.help: Optimisation steps of every fidelity sketch of the object for layers 8 and 11; shallower layers converge faster and use 60 % of it. Original: 1000 (600).
param.scenesketch.eval_interval.help: Every how many iterations the loss is evaluated and the best state is kept (fidelity sketches). Original: 50.
param.scenesketch.min_eval_iter.label: First evaluation
param.scenesketch.min_eval_iter.help: Iteration from which on the best state is tracked (earlier states are not used). Original: 400.
param.scenesketch.simplify_num_iter.help: Optimisation steps of every simplification level (per part). Original: 401.
param.scenesketch.background_divs.label: Simplification steps (background)
param.scenesketch.background_divs.help: Step size of the simplification per layer ("layer:step"). Every level halves the target ratio of strokes to CLIP loss 1/step times – larger steps remove strokes faster. Original: 2:0.35, 8:0.5, 11:0.85.
param.scenesketch.object_divs.label: Simplification steps (object)
param.scenesketch.object_divs.help: Like the background steps, for the object. Original: 2:0.4, 8:0.5, 11:0.9.
param.scenesketch.width_loss_weight.help: Weight of the loss that pushes towards fewer strokes during simplification. Original: 1.
param.scenesketch.width_lr.label: Learning rate (stroke removal)
param.scenesketch.width_lr.help: Learning rate of the network that decides which strokes to keep. Original: 0.00005.
param.scenesketch.gumbel_temp.label: Gumbel temperature
param.scenesketch.gumbel_temp.help: Temperature of the Gumbel-softmax that samples whether a stroke is kept. Smaller = harder decisions. Original: 0.2.
param.scenesketch.width.help: Width of every stroke in pixels on the 224 × 224 canvas. Original: 1.5.
Place the initial strokes of the object only inside the object mask. Original: off.
param.scenesketch.lr.label: Learning rate (positions)
param.scenesketch.lr.help: Learning rate of the network that moves the strokes (SceneSketch optimises an MLP instead of the points directly). Original: 0.0001.
param.scenesketch.save_interval.help: How often an intermediate state of each part is saved. The animation “drawing process” shows these steps: 1 = every iteration (the finest animation, more disk space with many parts), 100 = every hundredth (original). The CLIP score is computed about every 100 iterations either way.
ui.status.scene_inpaint: Filling in the background behind the object (LaMa) …
ui.warn.scene_no_object: No foreground object found – the whole scene is sketched as one.
ui.warn.scene_plain_background: The background is plain – only the object is sketched.
ui.matrix.empty: The matrix fills up while SceneSketch is running.
ui.models.group_hint.scenesketch: Downloaded on the first SceneSketch run that separates object and background.
ui.models.purpose.lama: LaMa inpainting – fills in the background behind the object.
ui.compare.scene_cpu_warning: SceneSketch takes hours per scene on the CPU. Compare with its “Fast” preset (one sketch, ≈ 20 min)?
ui.gallery.delete_q: Move “{name}” with all its sketches to the recycle bin?
ui.gallery.delete_permanently_q: “{name}” could not be moved to the recycle bin. Delete it permanently?
ui.export_desc.webp: Animated WebP of how the sketch is drawn – much smaller than a GIF and with a transparent background if you like; plays in all current browsers.
ui.export_webp_tip: Animated WebP: smaller than a GIF, transparent background possible
ui.export_matrix_tip: Every sketch of the SceneSketch matrix as SVG and PNG, plus an overview sheet – in one ZIP file.
ui.export_svglayers_tip: SVG with two layers, “Background” and “Object” – Inkscape and Illustrator open them as layers, e.g. to recolour or hide only the background.
ui.export_desc.svglayers: The scene as an SVG with two layers: “Background” (the strokes outside the object) and “Object”. Inkscape and Illustrator show them as layers of their own.
ui.layer.tip: Layers: show the whole sketch, only the background or only the object
ui.layer.not_yet: Layers: as soon as this cell is finished, background and object can be shown on their own
ui.export_desc.matrix: Every sketch of the matrix as SVG and PNG (L<layer>_level<n>), plus matrix.svg / matrix.png with all of them in one overview.
ui.settings.check_updates: Check for a new version on start
ui.settings.logs_tip: Error logs – attach them when you report a problem.
ui.diag.tip: Version, system, graphics card, folders, models and the last log lines – attach the text when you report a problem.
ui.selftest.title: Self-test
ui.selftest.desc: Short test runs of every method, continuing, the mask and loading the models – checks that everything works on this PC (about 2–5 minutes).
ui.selftest.failed: Something does not work – details below and in the log ({secs} s).
ui.selftest.busy: A job is running – wait until it is done, or cancel it.
ui.selftest.part.warm: Keep the models loaded between jobs
ui.backup.tip: Save the settings, the queue and the gallery (the models too, if wanted) in one file – to keep, or for a new computer
ui.backup.restore_tip: Put a backup back on this or a new computer
ui.backup.title: Make a backup
ui.backup.desc: Saves everything in a .clipbackup file: the settings, the queue with its pictures and the gallery – every sketch with its steps, names, notes and albums.
ui.backup.contents: Gallery: {jobs} results ({gallery}) · pictures of the queue: {queue}
ui.backup.with_models: Back up the downloaded models too ({size})
ui.backup.with_models_tip: Saves the download on the new computer – but makes the file much larger.
ui.backup.restore_desc: Backup of {created} (version {version}). What should come back?
ui.backup.restore_note: The folders of this computer stay (output and model folder). Results that are here already are skipped; nothing is overwritten.
ui.backup.restored: Done: {jobs} results back in the gallery ({skipped} were here already), {queue} jobs for the queue, {models} model files. Language and theme apply after a restart.
ui.backup.busy: Wait for the running job first, or pause it.
ui.backup.done_toast: Backup restored: {jobs} results, {queue} jobs in the queue
ui.phone.title: Phone & messages
ui.phone.desc: Control the app from your phone (in your own Wi-Fi) and get a Telegram message when a sketch is done.
ui.phone.remote_hint: Scan the QR code with the phone's camera: the phone then controls the studio – the picture (camera, gallery, files or from the PC), method, presets and own presets, every parameter, time budget, detail brush, start, pause and cancel, the live sketches, thumbs, exporting in every format (PNG, SVG, PDF, GIF, MP4, WebP, Lottie …, with all their settings), the gallery and the queue. Only reachable in the home network (or over Tailscale) and only after signing in with the QR code or the PIN; Windows asks about the firewall the first time – allow “Private networks”.
ui.phone.new_code_tip: Locks out phones that know the old QR code
ui.phone.pin_hint: Scanning the QR code signs the phone in at once. Keep the fixed address as a bookmark or on the home screen (“Add to Home Screen”): when the phone has forgotten the sign-in, the page asks for this PIN. The Tailscale address always stays the same, away from home, too; the home network address can change when the router gives the PC a new one.
ui.phone.qr_link: Link in the QR code (signs in directly):
ui.phone.tailscale_tip: Also lets in the devices of your Tailscale network (100.x addresses) – then the remote works away from home, too. The phone still has to sign in (QR code or PIN).
ui.phone.tailscale_hint: Scan the Tailscale QR code once with the phone (Tailscale must be connected on the phone). If it does not work, the Windows firewall usually blocks the Tailscale network – Windows often counts it as a “public network”: Windows Security → Firewall & network protection → “Allow an app through firewall” → tick “Public” for CLIPasso Studio, too.
ui.phone.tailscale_missing: Tailscale is not running on this PC right now – as soon as it is connected, the QR code with the Tailscale address appears here.
ui.phone.port_busy: Port {port} is in use – choose another one ({error}).
ui.phone.received: Picture from the phone: {name} – now in the studio
ui.phone.received_queue: Photo from the phone: {name} – in the queue
ui.phone.page.login_hint: Enter the 6-digit PIN – you find it on the PC under Settings → Phone & messages.
ui.phone.page.login_wait: Too many tries – please wait {s} s.
ui.phone.page.export_gone: This export is gone – please export again.
ui.phone.page.no_presets: No own presets yet. Set everything up and save it under a name – it is then in the app on the PC, too.
ui.phone.page.preset_placeholder: Name of the preset, e.g. Fine portrait
ui.phone.page.preset_save_hint: Saves the method and every parameter as they are set now – to be chosen on the PC under “My presets”, too. The same name updates the preset.
ui.phone.page.preset_replace_ask: Overwrite the preset “{name}” with the current settings?
ui.phone.page.no_background_yet: The background picture is made at the start of the job: SceneSketch cuts out the object and fills in the background behind it (LaMa).
ui.phone.page.matrix_hint: Tap a cell to see it large. Green frame: the best one.
ui.phone.page.mask_not_ready: The mask is still being computed – try again in a moment.
ui.phone.page.crop_hint: Drag the corners to crop, the frame to move it. The original stays; the crop is saved as a new picture.
ui.phone.page.download_ask: The comparison needs models that are missing. Download them on the PC now?
ui.phone.page.compare_hint: Sketch the studio's picture with several methods – the results appear here side by side, the best one with ★.
ui.phone.page.compare_none: Please choose at least one method.
ui.phone.page.viewer_hint: Swipe: next result · two fingers: zoom · double tap: back
ui.phone.page.uploaded_n: {ok} of {n} photos in the queue – with the studio's settings.
ui.phone.page.uploaded: The picture is in the studio.
ui.phone.page.models_missing: Models are missing for these settings (≈ {size} MB) – please download them on the PC under “Models”.
ui.phone.page.details_has: A detail map is saved for this picture.
ui.phone.page.details_not_used: (The chosen method does not use it – only CLIPasso and ControlSketch.)
ui.phone.page.face_found: Face found – the eyes, nose and mouth are marked.
ui.phone.page.reset_ask: Reset all parameters of this method?
ui.phone.page.started: Started – watch it in the “Sketch” tab.
ui.phone.page.no_sketch: No sketch yet – start one or open a result in the gallery.
ui.phone.page.no_live: No job is running right now.
ui.phone.page.delete_ask: Move “{name}” with all its sketches to the PC's recycle bin?
ui.phone.page.list_changed: The list has changed meanwhile – please try again.
ui.phone.page.busy: The app is busy right now – try again in a moment.
ui.telegram.label: Telegram message when done
ui.telegram.help: 1. In Telegram, create a bot with @BotFather (/newbot) and paste its token here. 2. Press “Connect” and send the bot /start. The token stays on this computer.
ui.telegram.send_start: Now send /start to your bot {bot} in Telegram (waiting {seconds} s) …
ui.telegram.bad_token: That does not look like a bot token (digits, a colon, letters).
ui.telegram.hello: CLIPasso Studio is connected ✓ – the finished sketches arrive here.
ui.report.tip: Prepares a bug report for GitHub – with the diagnostics. You see and can change everything first.
ui.report.title: Report a problem
ui.report.desc: This text is opened as a new issue on GitHub (you need a GitHub account). Paths with your user name are already shortened. Check the text and add what you did.
ui.report.opened: Opened in the browser – click “Submit new issue” there. The text is in the clipboard as well.
ui.report.cut: Opened in the browser. The text was too long for the address and was cut – the full text is in the clipboard and can be pasted there.
ui.resources.title: The memory may not be enough for this
ui.resources.ram: RAM: needs about {need} GB, {free} GB are free.
ui.resources.vram: Graphics memory: needs about {need} GB, {free} GB are usable.
ui.resources.no_smaller: There are no smaller settings for this. It can still be started – Windows then swaps to the disk, which is slow.
ui.budget.label: Time budget
ui.budget.tip: Choose the settings so the job takes about this long on this computer – with the best sketch to expect (iterations, number, turbo, augmentations; from the measured times)
ui.budget.title: Time budget
ui.budget.ask: How many minutes may the job take?
ui.budget.too_short: It cannot be quite that short – the quickest variant takes about {time}; it is set.
ui.update.available: CLIPasso Studio {version} is available – you have {current}.

CLIPasso Studio keeps running, but the last action may not have finished. The details were saved in:

ui.crash.last_time: CLIPasso Studio closed unexpectedly last time.
ui.crash.last_time_text:
A log was saved – it helps to find the cause:
{path}
ui.shortcut.paste: Paste an image from the clipboard
ui.shortcut.export: Export the sketch (in the format used last; SVG at first)
ui.shortcut.focus: Focus mode: the canvas alone, full screen (Esc ends it)
ui.focus.enter: Focus mode: the canvas alone, full screen (F11)
ui.timelapse.play: Time-lapse: shows how the sketch came about (arrow: speed)
ui.sheet.empty: All sketches of the job appear here side by side.
ui.sheet.make_best: Choose as the best sketch (the job's result)
ui.sheet.best_set: New best sketch chosen – the gallery, exports and the phone take it now.
ui.history.title: Earlier sketches of this photo ({n})
ui.viewer.title: Large view
ui.viewer.slideshow_tip: Show the results one after another by themselves (Space)
ui.viewer.slideshow_gallery_tip: Show the shown results large one after another – ←/→ to go on, Space pauses
ui.viewer.interval_tip: How long each result stays in the slideshow
ui.viewer.compare_tip: The two marked results on top of each other – drag the divider to switch between them
ui.viewer.zoom_tip: Mouse wheel: zoom · drag: move · double click: zoom in / show whole · ←/→: browse
ui.viewer.split_tip: Drag: divider · mouse wheel: zoom · Shift+←/→: move the divider step by step
ui.hint.small: The photo is very small ({w}×{h} px). Below {min} px it is enlarged and the sketch gets less exact – a bigger photo helps.
ui.hint.dark: The photo is very dark – outlines get lost easily. A brighter photo helps (or brighten it first).
ui.hint.flat: The photo has little contrast – the object hardly stands out. More contrast or a calm background helps.
ui.hint.blurry: The photo looks blurred – fine lines become unsure. A sharper photo helps.
ui.hint.small_object: The object is very small in the picture (about {percent} % of it). Cropping gives it more strokes.
ui.hint.no_object: No object was found in the picture – the whole picture is drawn. Check the mask or paint the object in yourself.
ui.hint.unsure_mask: The mask is unsure (for {percent} % of its pixels) – check it before you start.
ui.hint.dismissed: This hint won't come again. You can switch it back on in the settings.
ui.work.tip_output: The results are moving to the new folder. You can keep working – new jobs start afterwards, the gallery is locked meanwhile.
ui.work.tip_models: The models are moving to the new folder. You can keep working – jobs and downloads start afterwards.
ui.work.tip_update: The update is being unpacked in the background. You can keep working.
ui.work.job_waits: The job waits in the queue and starts as soon as the move is done.
ui.work.gallery_locked: The results are being moved to the new folder – the gallery is back in a moment.
ui.work.models_locked: The models are being moved – downloads work as soon as that is done.
ui.work.output_done: The results are in the new folder.
ui.work.models_done: The models are in the new folder.
ui.work.quit_wait: Files are being moved or unpacked right now. Please wait until that is done (the progress is shown at the top of the window) – otherwise half a folder would be left behind.
ui.update.placed_q: The update is unpacked. Restart now?
ui.update.on_close: The update starts when you close the app.
ui.gallery.empty_how: Choose a photo in the studio and start a sketch. Every finished sketch lands here – a double click opens it again, Space shows it large.
ui.gallery.empty_match: No result fits the search, filter or album.
ui.compare.empty: Load a photo in the studio. The chosen methods then draw it one after another here, and you see the results side by side – the best one marked.
ui.resume.running: This job was interrupted – {done} of {total} sketches are finished. Continue where it stopped?
ui.resume.interrupted: This job was interrupted – {done} of {total} sketches are finished. Continue where it stopped?
ui.resume.cancelled: This job was cancelled – {done} of {total} sketches are finished. Continue where it stopped?
ui.resume.failed: This job stopped because of an error – {done} of {total} sketches are finished. Try to continue?
ui.resume.queued: The job continues where it stopped.
ui.resume.nothing: This job is already queued or has nothing left to do.
ui.resume.startup_title: Unfinished work from the last session ({n}): the app was closed or crashed while it was running.
ui.resume.startup_text: Finished sketches are kept; the rest continues from the last checkpoint.
ui.brush.label: Style
ui.brush.tip: How the strokes are drawn: plain lines, tapered ink, soft pencil, grainy charcoal or chalk, ballpoint pen, a wide marker, watercolour washes, glowing neon or calligraphy with a broad nib.
ui.paper.label: Paper
ui.paper.tip: A texture under the sketch – made by the app and part of every export (PNG, PDF, GIF, MP4, WebP, SVG). Its colour is the background colour; on a dark paper black strokes become light. GIF files get larger with it.
ui.eraser.tip: Eraser: click or drag over strokes to remove them (the stroke under the cursor turns red). The original stays; exports use the touched-up sketch.
ui.edit_bar.history_tip: Take a saved step: go through the saved steps of the sketch and make one of them the result
ui.edit_bar.history_note: Drag through the saved steps – “Take it” makes the one shown the result. Can be undone; the original stays.
ui.edit_bar.no_steps: No steps were saved for this sketch.
ui.edit_bar.simplify_tip: Simplify: leave out the least important strokes first (measured with CLIP)
ui.edit_bar.simplify_note: Drag to the left: the strokes that add the least to the picture go first (measured with CLIP).
ui.edit_bar.measuring: CLIP is measuring how much each stroke adds … (a few seconds, once per sketch)
ui.edit_bar.exit_code: the measuring process ended with code {code}
ui.rate.up: Thumbs up: I like this sketch (click again to take it back). From 10 ratings on, “Best sketch: My taste” learns from them.
ui.rate.down: Thumbs down: I don’t like this sketch (click again to take it back).
ui.rate.progress: Noted – {n} more rating(s), then “My taste” knows you
ui.rate.learnt: Noted – “My taste” now learns from {n} ratings
ui.rate.need_both: Noted – “My taste” also needs sketches you don’t like (and the other way round)
ui.rate.failed: The sketch could not be measured – the rating counts later
ui.taste.label: My taste
ui.taste.tip: Learnt from your thumbs up/down in the studio. Choose “My taste” under “Best sketch” to let it decide too.
ui.taste.forget_q: Forget the learnt taste? The thumbs on the sketches stay visible but only count again once you set them anew.
ui.eraser.revert: Back to the sketch as it was drawn
ui.edit_image.tip: Crop, rotate or flip the image (saved as a copy; the original stays)
ui.detail.title: Detail brush
ui.detail.hint: Paint where the sketch should get more detail (orange) and where less (blue). CLIPasso and ControlSketch put more starting strokes there and draw the blue areas more loosely. The map belongs to this image – in the queue and when continuing, too.
ui.detail.face_tip: Portrait mode: finds a face and marks the eyes, nose and mouth as “more detail” (BlazeFace face detection, runs on this computer).
ui.detail.share: More detail: {more} % · less: {less} % of the image
ui.detail.no_face: No face found – paint the areas yourself
ui.detail.saved: Detail map saved – it applies from the next start
ui.detail.tip: Detail brush: more or less detail in particular places (with portrait mode)
ui.detail.has: A detail map is saved for this image.
ui.detail.not_used: The chosen method does not use the map (only CLIPasso and ControlSketch).
ui.edit_image.title: Edit the image
ui.queue.add_folder_tip: Add every image of a folder to the queue (with the current settings of the studio)
ui.queue.subfolders_q: Also add the images in its subfolders?
ui.queue.folder_empty: No images found in this folder.
ui.batch.title: Export several sketches
ui.batch.desc: The best sketch of each of the {n} results is exported into one folder (touched-up sketches as edited).
ui.batch.nothing: There are no finished results to export.
ui.batch.export_all_tip: Export the finished results of the queue at once
ui.batch.export_shown_tip: Export every result shown (use the filters to choose, e.g. favourites)
param.controlsketch.mask_object.help: Removes the background and sketches only the object, scaled to “Object size” (like the original, which always does this). Off: the whole picture including the background is sketched.
ui.settings.ui_scale_tip: Makes the whole interface smaller or larger – for small laptop screens or large monitors.
ui.settings.restart_hint: The new size is used after a restart.
ui.update.install_desc: The new version is downloaded ({mb} MB) and checked. Downloaded models, settings and results are kept.
ui.update.ready: CLIPasso Studio {version} is ready to install.
ui.update.ready_installed: CLIPasso Studio closes, installs the update and starts again.
ui.update.ready_portable: The new version is saved next to this one and starts now; you can delete the old exe afterwards.
ui.update.ready_portable-zip: The new version is unpacked next to this folder and starts now; it then offers to delete the old folder.
param.mask_model.label: Mask model
param.mask_model.help: The network that finds the object. BiRefNet is by far the most precise (fine details, several objects, busy backgrounds); it is downloaded once (444 MB) and takes a few seconds per image on a CPU. BiRefNet lite: faster and smaller (89 MB), slightly less precise. U²-Net: included, the mask of the original CLIPasso.
ui.models.purpose.birefnet: Precise object mask (background removal) for all methods – the default.
ui.models.purpose.blazeface: Finds faces for the portrait mode of the detail brush (0.4 MB).
ui.models.group_hint.masking: BiRefNet finds the object much more precisely than U²-Net. Downloaded on the first run that removes the background (Hugging Face); “Mask model” in the settings picks the network.
ui.mask.show: Show the mask on the image
ui.mask.edit: Edit the mask: remove parts or add what it missed
ui.mask_edit.title: Edit mask
ui.mask_edit.hint: The veiled area is removed before sketching. Click a part to remove it, or click outside the mask to add an area (similar colours are selected). Paint with the brush for everything else.
ui.mask_edit.reset_tip: Back to the mask of the mask model
ui.mask_edit.share: The object covers {pct} % of the image
ui.mask_edit.empty: The mask is empty – add a part or paint the object
ui.mask_edit.nothing_here: Nothing found here – paint it with the brush (Add)
param.frame_object.label: Fit the object
param.frame_object.help: Small objects are enlarged so they fill the picture: the image is cropped around the mask with a margin. Only with “Remove background”; objects that already fill the picture stay as they are. Not in the original (where small objects get small sketches).
ui.export_mode.label: Animation
ui.export_mode.tip: Drawing process: how the optimisation shapes the sketch. Stroke by stroke: the finished strokes are drawn one after another, like by hand.
ui.export_svganim_tip: An SVG that draws itself stroke by stroke in the browser – for websites
ui.export_desc.svganim: The finished sketch draws itself stroke by stroke and starts again after the pause – in every browser, on websites and in presentations (CSS animation; image editors show the finished sketch).
ui.export_lottie_tip: Lottie animation (JSON) for websites and apps – lottie-web, LottieFiles, After Effects
ui.export_desc.lottie: The sketch draws itself stroke by stroke – as a Lottie file for websites, apps (iOS, Android) and After Effects: one layer per stroke, sharp at any size. Lottie has no brush styles: the strokes stay plain lines; the background or the paper lies below them.
ui.export_html_tip: A web page of its own (HTML) on which the sketch draws itself – to send or upload
ui.export_desc.html: A web page in a single file: the sketch draws itself on it stroke by stroke, with its brush style and paper, and a button draws it again. Opens in every browser, also on a phone.
ui.print.title: Print & print layout
ui.print.desc: Lay out {n} sketch(es) on pages – one per page or as a contact sheet, with a title and a signature. Save as a PDF or print right away.
ui.print.heading: Title
ui.print.captions: Write the names under the sketches
ui.print.tip: Print layout: page size, margins, title and signature – as a PDF or straight to the printer
ui.export_desc.pdf: Vector PDF for printing – sharp at any size; the page has the shape of the sketch.
ui.copy_tip: Puts the sketch on the clipboard (image and SVG) with your last export choices – paste it into Word, PowerPoint, Figma, Photoshop …
ui.drop_many.title: Several images
ui.drop_many.text: You dropped {n} images. The first one is open in the studio – add all of them to the queue with the current settings?
ui.queue.when_done_tip: What the PC does after the last job of the queue – for runs overnight. Only for this session; a countdown lets you stop it.
ui.queue.done_text_sleep: The PC goes to sleep in {s} s.
ui.queue.done_text_shutdown: The PC shuts down in {s} s. Your sketches are saved.
ui.settings.models_hint: {size} of downloaded models here. The models included with the app stay where they are.
ui.settings.models_busy: Wait until the running sketch is done, then change the model folder.
ui.settings.models_nested: The new folder must not be inside the old one (or the other way round).
ui.settings.models_move_q: Move your downloaded models ({size}) to the new folder?
ui.settings.models_no_space: Not enough free space in the new folder for {size}.
ui.settings.output_move_q:
Take your results ({n} folders, {size}) along to the new output folder?
Other files in the old folder stay where they are.
ui.settings.output_busy: The output folder cannot be changed while a sketch is being computed – it is writing into it.
ui.storage.title: Storage
ui.storage.desc: Caches and leftovers – everything here can be cleared safely. Your sketches and models stay.
ui.storage.masks_tip: Object masks computed before; they are computed again when needed.
ui.storage.thumbs_tip: Thumbnails of the gallery; they are made again the next time.
ui.storage.updates_tip: Setup files of updates; installed ones are removed at the start anyway.
ui.storage.inputs_tip: Images from the clipboard, the webcam, cropping and "Continue" (folders _pasted, _webcam, _edited, _continued). Jobs keep their own copy of the image; images the queue still waits for stay.
ui.storage.clear_q.thumbs: Delete the thumbnails? They are made again when needed.
ui.storage.clear_q.inputs: Delete pasted, captured and edited images? Your sketches keep their own copy of the image.
ui.gpurt.title: Graphics card add-on
ui.gpurt.dialog_desc: PyTorch with CUDA 12.6 for older NVIDIA cards (GTX 9xx / 10xx): {download} GB download, {disk} GB on the disk. Afterwards CLIPasso Studio computes on your graphics card.
ui.gpurt.restart: Done. Restart CLIPasso Studio so that it uses your graphics card.
ui.gpurt.offer: Your graphics card ({gpu}) is not supported by this version directly – CLIPasso Studio is computing on the processor.
ui.gpurt.offer_again: The add-on for your graphics card ({gpu}) has to be downloaded again for this version.
ui.gpurt.offer_text: With an add-on (PyTorch with CUDA 12.6: {download} GB download, {disk} GB on the disk) the app computes on the graphics card instead of the processor. Download it now?
ui.gpurt.state_missing: Add-on not installed. Needed for NVIDIA cards older than the GTX 16xx ({download} GB download).
ui.gpurt.remove_q: Delete the add-on ({disk} GB)? The app then computes on the processor again.
ui.gpurt.removed_later: The add-on is still in use and will be deleted at the next start.
ui.gpurt.precision_tip: Off (default): Stable Diffusion, ControlNet, BLIP and BiRefNet compute in fp16 on the graphics card – half the graphics memory, the same pictures. On: everything in fp32 – twice the graphics memory and usually slower; only to compare, or if a card computes wrongly with fp16. Applies from the next job.
ui.settings.sdxl_small_gpu: SDXL on graphics cards below 8 GB
ui.settings.sdxl_small_gpu.tip: ControlSketch's optional SDXL attention needs about 7 GB of graphics memory. On a smaller card this step computes piece by piece on the card (the pieces wait in the RAM, about 9 GB) or entirely on the processor (slow, about 15 GB) – or CLIP is used instead.
param.sdxl_place.label: SDXL on graphics cards below 8 GB
param.sdxl_place.help: Where SDXL computes when the graphics card has less than 8 GB: piece by piece on the card (faster; the pieces wait in the RAM) or entirely on the processor. No effect on bigger cards.
ui.tour.methods.title: Four ways to sketch
ui.tour.methods.text: CLIPasso: the classic for single objects, very configurable (minutes). SwiftSketch: an object in seconds. ControlSketch: the most detailed object sketches (best with a GPU). SceneSketch: whole scenes with background, in several levels of abstraction.
ui.tour.input.title: Your picture
ui.tour.input.text: Drop a photo here, open one or paste it (Ctrl+V) – several images or a folder go to the queue. Crop it with the frame icon. The object the method will sketch is shown on the image; with the brush icon you can fix the mask.
ui.tour.params.title: Settings
ui.tour.params.text: Start with a preset – Fast, Standard or Quality. Every option of the original methods is here, each with an explanation; search finds any of them.
ui.tour.start.title: Draw
ui.tour.start.text: “Create sketch” starts right away and shows the drawing live (Ctrl+Enter). “To queue” collects images to run one after another – e.g. overnight; the queue can even put the PC to sleep when it is done.
ui.tour.result.title: Use the result
ui.tour.result.text: Export the sketch as SVG, PNG or PDF, as an animation (also stroke by stroke) or copy it (Ctrl+C) – with brush styles like ink or pencil. Single strokes can be erased in the sketch view.
ui.tour.gallery.title: Queue and gallery
ui.tour.gallery.text: The queue shows what is running and waiting. The gallery keeps every result: open one to continue with its image and settings, mark favourites, or continue interrupted jobs.
ui.tour.models.title: Models and settings
ui.tour.models.text: SwiftSketch, ControlSketch, SceneSketch and the precise BiRefNet mask download their models on first use – here you can see and manage them. The settings have the theme, language, interface size and the folders. This guide is on the About page.

ui.export_every_step_tip: Sets the length so that each saved step of the drawing process gets its own frame. How many steps there are is set before the run: “Save a step every … iterations” (1 = every iteration).
ui.settings.parallel: Compute several sketches at once on a big CPU
ui.settings.parallel_tip: CLIPasso and SwiftSketch: with 6 or more CPU cores and enough free memory, the sketches of a job run side by side instead of one after the other (each with its share of the cores). Not used on a GPU.
ui.settings.multi_gpu_tip: The sketches of a job are spread over all graphics cards, one sketch per card at the same time (CLIPasso, SwiftSketch, ControlSketch).
ui.settings.keep_models: Keep the models loaded between jobs
ui.settings.keep_models_tip: The next job of the queue starts without loading PyTorch and the models again (saves 5–60 s per job). They stay in memory until 5 minutes after the last job.

param.turbo.label: Turbo mode
param.turbo.help: Faster, with a slightly different result: the CLIP features of the augmented input are computed only once, with several sketches only the best one continues after a quarter of the iterations, and a sketch stops as soon as it hardly improves any more.
param.controlsketch.turbo.help: Faster, with a slightly different result: the sketch is encoded with the small TAESD autoencoder (10 MB download) instead of the Stable Diffusion VAE and drawn on a 384 px canvas instead of 512 px (it looks the same at the end); on CPUs with bfloat16 support (AVX-512 BF16 or AMX) Stable Diffusion also runs in bfloat16.
param.scenesketch.turbo.help: Faster, with a slightly different result: the CLIP features of the augmented input are computed only once, with two or more sketches per part only the better one continues after a quarter of the iterations, and a fidelity sketch stops as soon as it hardly improves any more.
ui.log.plateau: Sketch {seed} hardly improved any more – stopped at iteration {it} (turbo mode)
ui.models.purpose.taesd: Small autoencoder for the turbo mode of ControlSketch (instead of the Stable Diffusion VAE).

ui.pen.tip: Pen: draw your own strokes into the sketch (they stay as they are when CLIPasso continues the sketch)
ui.continue.title: Continue with CLIPasso
ui.continue.desc: Starts a new CLIPasso job with this sketch as its beginning: its strokes are improved further and new ones can be added. The original sketch stays as it is.
ui.continue.keep: Keep my {n} drawn strokes as they are
ui.continue.keep_tip: Strokes you drew with the pen stay exactly as they are; only the other strokes move.
ui.continue.no_input: The input image of this sketch (input.png) is missing – it cannot be continued.
ui.continue.queued: Added to the queue – CLIPasso continues the sketch
param.one_line.label: One line
param.one_line.help: Draws the whole sketch as one continuous line: a single smooth path through the most important points of the picture, in the order of a short route. Strokes, segments and stages are then set by this mode.
param.one_line_segments.label: Line segments
param.one_line_segments.help: Number of curve pieces of the one line: fewer give a calm, abstract line, more give a detailed one with many turns.
ui.frame.label: Shape
ui.frame.tip: Shape of the exported picture: the square canvas the sketch was drawn on, the shape of the original photo (the sketch where the object is in the photo), or tightly cropped to the strokes. The strokes stay vectors.
ui.frame.photo_unknown: Not known for this sketch: the object was zoomed in on (a sketch from before 3.0)
ui.frame.margin_tip: Free space around the strokes, as a share of the sketch's longer side

ui.gallery.keys_tip: Double click or Enter: open · Space: view large · Ctrl/Shift or drag on an empty spot: select several · drag sketches onto an album: add them · F: favourite · Del: delete · Ctrl+A: all

ui.watch.title: Watched folder
ui.watch.desc: Images saved into this folder are sketched by themselves (as soon as they are completely written) and exported when they are done – handy for a camera, a scanner or a sync folder. Images already handled are not sketched again.
